h: Stars Sand and Dust Reveal the Worth of Yisrael

p: after the rebuke of Parshas Bechukosai,
so that the year and its curses may end.
And likewise Parshas Nitzavim is read
after the rebuke in Mishneh Torah,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּכְלֶה הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלֵּי
which is likewise so that the year may end, etc.,
That is, after the rebuke we read,
אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים הַיּוֹם כּוּלְּכֶם וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים כט, ט)
"You are standing today, all of you" etc. (Devarim 29:9);
for after the rebuke and the sufferings,
all the individual souls of Yisrael were clarified,
that all of them have a root in holiness.
all the individual souls were clarified,
and all of them are included in the root of holiness,
as stated in the holy Zohar (beginning of this parsha, III 117a):
the hosts of the Torah and the hosts of the Mishkan.
For all of them are hosts of the Mishkan,
since the offerings came from the half-shekels
of every individual soul of Yisrael.
And all of them are also hosts of the Torah,
עַל פָּסוּק אֶל כָּל קְהַלְכֶם (דְּבָרִים ה, יט)
on the pasuk "to all your congregation" (Devarim 5:19),
one soul of Yisrael been missing,
the Torah would not have been given to them.
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה ב, יב)
And it is stated in the Midrash Rabbah on this parsha (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:12),
עַל פָּסוּק וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
on the pasuk "And the number of the Bnei Yisrael shall be"
that Yisrael were blessed with three blessings:
like the stars, like the sand, and like the dust of the earth.
The blessing of the stars was given to Avraham:
וְהִרְבֵּיתִי אֶת זַרְעֲךָ כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם (בְּרֵאשִׁית כו, ד)
"And I will multiply your seed like the stars of the heavens" (Bereishis 26:4),
And the blessing of the sand was given to Yitzchak:
וְכַחוֹל אֲשֶׁר עַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם (שָׁם כב, יז)
"and like the sand that is on the seashore" (Bereishis 22:17).
And the blessing of the dust was given to Yaakov:
וְהָיָה זַרְעֲךָ כַּעֲפַר הָאָרֶץ (שָׁם כח, יד)
"and your seed shall be like the dust of the earth" (Bereishis 28:14).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is because the aspect of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to lift his eyes on high
with great longing to cleave to Him, Yisbarach.
And corresponding to this he was told,
And the aspect of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
to be a mighty one who conquers his inclination;
therefore he was given the blessing of the sand
as stated in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Chukas)
עַל פָּסוּק וַיִּתֵּן ה׳ חָכְמָה לִשְׁלֹמֹה
on the pasuk "And Hashem gave Shlomo wisdom
כְּחוֹל שֶׁעַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם (מְלָכִים א ה, ט)
like the sand that is on the seashore" (Melachim I 5:9):
just as the sand is a fence for the sea,
was a fence against his inclination.
For the waters of the sea allude
to the desires of the opposite side,
"like the roaring of the seas they roar";
and through the blessing of the sand
every individual soul has the strength
And the blessing of the dust of the earth
was given to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
שֶׁגַּם אִם חָלִילָה שׁוּם נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
that even if, Heaven forbid, some soul of Yisrael
should be sunk at the lowest level,
down to the dust, Heaven forbid,
and take refuge in the Name of Hashem

p: It says further there in the Midrash:
the blessing of the stars was fulfilled
in the days of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him:
וְהִנְּכֶם הַיּוֹם כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם לָרוֹב (דְּבָרִים א, י)
"and behold you are today like the stars of the heavens in multitude" (Devarim 1:10);
and the blessing of the sand in the days of Hoshea:
וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם
"And the number of the Bnei Yisrael shall be like the sand of the sea";
and the blessing of the dust in the days of Bilam:
מִי מָנָה עֲפַר יַעֲקֹב (בְּמִדְבַּר כג, י)
"Who has counted the dust of Yaakov?" (Bamidbar 23:10).
It says further there, a parable:
one who has three crafts in his hand,
this is Moshe, who likened them to stars.
this is Bilam, who likened them to dust.
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא אוֹהֵב וְלֹא שׂוֹנֵא
And whoever neither loves nor hates him
this is Hoshea, who likened them to sand.
were not the days of Moshe and the days of Bilam
at one and the same time?
וְגַם יְמֵי הוֹשֵׁעַ מַאן דְּכַר שְׁמֵיהּ
And also, who mentioned the days of Hoshea?
הֲלֹא בְּרָכַת וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
The blessing "And the number of the Bnei Yisrael shall be"
refers to the future to come!
וְגַם אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר עַל הוֹשֵׁעַ
And also, how can one say of Hoshea,
who was a prophet of Yisrael,
that he was not a lover, Heaven forbid?
But all this can be understood
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכְּבָר דִּבַּרְנוּ מִזֶּה
according to what we have already discussed,
from the question of the Arizal, of blessed memory
(Likkutei Torah of the Arizal, Parshas Balak),
עַל פָּסוּק תָּמוּת נַפְשִׁי מוֹת יְשָׁרִים (בְּמִדְבַּר כג, י)
on the pasuk "May my soul die the death of the upright" (Bamidbar 23:10):
after all, it was not fulfilled in him,
so how was this written in the Torah?
that in truth it was fulfilled
who have no share in the World to Come.
כִּי זֶהוּ הָיָה בַּקָּשַׁת בִּלְעָם עַל נַפְשׁוֹ
For this was Bilam's request for his soul:
that at least "may my soul die,"
that is, the death of the soul,
which has no share in the World to Come,
together with "the death of the upright,"
that is, the lowest among the souls of Yisrael,
who have no share in the World to Come.
כִּי בִלְעָם לֹא הָיָה לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה
of the precious souls in Yisrael,
only of those that are low like the dust of the earth,
who have no share in the World to Come.
all of them come to the World to Come."
הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
means one who has a bond with the root,
which is alluded to in the markings,
that even the souls of Yisrael
that sank to the lowest level
have a bond with the root of holiness,
and there all the sins become merits,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים
as it says, "If your sins be like the years,"
and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos 89b):
"Like these years that come in order
from the six days of Creation,
they shall be made white as snow."
And they did not count Bilam among them,
where it is explained at length).
Now Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הָיָה אוֹהֵב לְכָל פְּרָטֵי נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
loved every individual soul of Yisrael,
because he perceived the preciousness of all of them,
how they cleave to the root;
therefore he said to them, "and behold you,"
that sank to the lowest level, down to the dust,
have a bond with the root,
like the stars of the heavens.
And one may say that it is for this allusion
that it is mentioned in the rebuke of Mishneh Torah,
שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ אֲמָרָן (מְגִילָּה לא, ב)
which Moshe said on his own (Megillah 31b),
that is, according to the root of his perception:
"The stranger who is in your midst
shall rise above you higher and higher,
and you shall go down" etc. (Devarim 28:43).
and as stated in the Zohar Chadash (Parshas Tavo),
that the rebukes in Mishneh Torah
allude to the destruction of the Second Temple,
which took place at the beginning of the era of the Tanna'im.
עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
through the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
that sank in the depths of the kelipos.
And this is "the stranger who is in your midst
it alludes to the soul of Rabbi Akiva,
who was the son of converts,
and his soul was from the Shevatim, as is known,
and it had sunk specifically into the depths of the kelipah;
the root of the power of Torah she'b'al peh,
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ כִּתְרֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת (מְנָחוֹת כט, ב)
as is known that he would expound the crowns of the letters (Menachos 29b),
עַד שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
until Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, said
that the Torah should be given through him;
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Menachos 29b):
"Be silent; so it arose in thought."
וְהִנֵּה זֶהוּ הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Now this is the perception of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him:
even one who has sunk into the depths of the kelipah,
to return him to the root of holiness, as mentioned above;
וְלָכֵן קִיבֵּל גַּם הָעֵרֶב רַב כַּיָּדוּעַ
and therefore he also accepted the Erev Rav, as is known.
But in this rebuke of Toras Kohanim,
only the number of the Bnei Yisrael alone,
And regarding the future to come it says
כִּי גַּם הַגֵּרִים יִהְיֶה לָהֶם חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ
that the converts too will have a portion in the Land.
whose perception was according to the Torah,
that one who sees his fellow
he is called neither a lover nor a hater,
כְּדְאִיתָא בְּהַתַּנְיָא מֵהָרַב זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
as stated in the Tanya of the Rav, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
to hate the portion of evil within him,
caused by the leaven in the dough,
וְעִם כׇּל זֶה לֶאֱהוֹב אוֹתוֹ כְּנַפְשׁוֹ
and nevertheless to love him like himself
on account of the portion of holiness
to the sand that is on the seashore;
for at least this is the virtue
that he saw even in the lowly souls of Yisrael:
that they have the power to prevail
even if they have already descended
down to the dust, Heaven forbid,
that the sand is a fence for the sea.
